name: Odoo 14-18 (JSON-RPC)
description: Odoo ERP 14 to 18 over the classic JSON-RPC endpoint: search, read, create and update any model, plus partners, sales orders, invoices and products. For Odoo Online, Odoo.sh and self-hosted Odoo older than 19 (works on 19 too). API key + user id.
instructions:
**Which Odoo connector?** This one is for **Odoo 14 to 18** (and works on 19 too). It talks to Odoo's classic JSON-RPC endpoint `/jsonrpc`. For Odoo 19 and newer, the "Odoo" connector (JSON-2 API) is the simpler choice: it needs no user id. Your version is shown at the bottom of **Settings**.

**What you need (four values)**
1. `ODOO_URL`: the address of your Odoo, scheme and host only, e.g. `https://erp.example.com` or `https://mycompany.odoo.com`. Not the address of a page inside Odoo: nothing after the host, no `/web`, no `?db=` or `#action=`.
2. `ODOO_DB`: the database name. On Odoo Online it is usually the subdomain. On your own server it is the name shown on the database selector, or the value after `?db=` in the address bar.
3. `ODOO_API_KEY`: in Odoo open your user menu → **Preferences** (Odoo 14/15: **My Profile**) → **Account Security** → **New API Key**. Odoo shows the key once. If the Account Security tab or the API key button is missing, turn on developer mode (Settings → Activate the developer mode). The key replaces your password for API calls; your login password itself also works but is not recommended.
4. `ODOO_UID`: the numeric id of the Odoo user the key belongs to. Open **Settings → Users & Companies → Users**, open that user, and read the number after `id=` in the address bar (e.g. `...#id=7&model=res.users` → `7`).

The key, the user id and the database must belong together: a key of user 7 with `ODOO_UID=2` is refused.

**Errors**: Odoo answers JSON-RPC errors inside an HTTP 200 with an `error` object. AnythingMCP raises them as errors carrying Odoo's own message: `Access Denied` (wrong key, user id or database), `Invalid field 'x' on model 'y'` (field names differ between versions), `Record does not exist`.

**Domains are Odoo's query language.** A domain is a list of triples: `[["state","=","sale"],["amount_total",">",1000]]`, implicitly AND-ed. `|` and `!` prefix operators express OR and NOT.

**Always pass `fields`** to `odoo_search_read` and `odoo_read`: Odoo models have hundreds of columns. Start with `odoo_fields_get` to see what exists; field names differ between Odoo versions (e.g. `mobile` on res.partner is gone in 19).

**Permissions follow the user.** The key inherits its owner's access rights and record rules. A restricted user sees fewer rows, not an error.

**Self-hosted**: on **AnythingMCP Cloud** the instance must be reachable from the public internet with a valid TLS certificate. On an internal host, self-host AnythingMCP on the same network and add the host to `SSRF_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.

**Writes**: `odoo_create`, `odoo_write` and `odoo_call_method` change the live database, and Odoo's automations fire as if a person had done it.

tools.name: odoo_search_read
tools.description: Search and read any Odoo model in one call. The general-purpose tool: pass a model, an Odoo domain and the fields you want. Always name the fields — Odoo models have hundreds of columns.

model.description: Technical model name, e.g. res.partner, sale.order, account.move, product.product.

domain.description: Odoo domain as a list of triples, e.g. [["state","=","sale"]]. Empty list matches everything.

fields.description: Field names to return. Omitting this returns every column.

tools.name: odoo_read
tools.description: Read specific records of a model by their ids — the follow-up call when a search has returned ids and you now want the detail of a few of them.

tools.name: odoo_search_count
tools.description: Count the records of a model matching a domain, without transferring them. Use this before a search_read to find out whether the answer is 12 rows or 120,000.

domain.description: Odoo domain as a list of triples. Required by Odoo; pass [] to count every record.

tools.name: odoo_fields_get
tools.description: Describe a model's fields: name, type, label, whether it is required or readonly, and the related model for relational fields. Read this before composing a domain against an unfamiliar model.

tools.name: odoo_list_partners
tools.description: List partners — Odoo's customers, suppliers and contacts — with name, e-mail, phone, city and country. Convenience wrapper over res.partner.

domain.description: Extra Odoo domain, e.g. [["customer_rank",">",0]] for customers only.

tools.name: odoo_list_sale_orders
tools.description: List sales orders with their customer, date, state and total. Convenience wrapper over sale.order; state `sale` means confirmed, `draft` a quotation.

tools.name: odoo_list_invoices
tools.description: List customer invoices and vendor bills with their partner, date, due date, state and residual amount — the answer to 'what is still unpaid'.

tools.name: odoo_list_products
tools.description: List products with their internal reference, sale price, cost, product type and unit of measure. Convenience wrapper over product.product. Stock on hand (`qty_available`) only exists when the Inventory app is installed, so it is not requested here: ask for it with odoo_search_read on product.product when the database has Inventory.

tools.name: odoo_create
tools.description: Create a record in any Odoo model and return its id. Writes to the live database and fires Odoo's automations: mail, stock moves and accounting entries all behave as if a person had done it.

values.description: Field values for the new record, e.g. {"name": "Muster GmbH", "email": "info@muster.de"}.

tools.name: odoo_write
tools.description: Update existing records in any Odoo model. Writes to the live database; a domain that matches more rows than you expected will update all of them.

ids.description: Ids of the records to update.

tools.name: odoo_call_method
tools.description: Call a public method on an Odoo model: the escape hatch for workflow actions such as action_confirm on a sale order, action_post on an invoice or activity_schedule on a lead.

method.description: Public method name, e.g. action_confirm, action_post, message_post, activity_schedule, name_search.

args.description: Positional arguments. For a method that acts on records (action_confirm, action_post, message_post, activity_schedule) the FIRST argument is the list of record ids, e.g. [[42]]. For a model-level method (name_search, default_get) pass its own arguments, e.g. ["Acme"].

kwargs.description: Keyword arguments by name, e.g. {"summary": "Call back", "date_deadline": "2026-10-16"} for activity_schedule.
